items.title: Chennai: 71.24 kg heroin worth Rs 140 crore seized from ice cream vending vehicle
items.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized around 71.24 kg of heroin, worth Rs 140 crore, from an ice cream vending vehicle near Madhavaram in Chennai on Tuesday, November 17. Two men have been arrested in connection with the seizure and remanded to judicial custody. The accused have been identified as Abdul Shukkur (32) and his brother-in-law Shafiq Ahmed (30), both natives of southern Tamil Nadu who were residing in Chennai. According to reports, the DRI received specific intelligence inputs on Monday night about a large consignment of narcotics being smuggled from abroad and being transported through vehicles in Chennai suburbs. Following the tip-off, special teams were formed and surveillance was intensified near Chennai airport and along the Chennai-Tiruchy and Chennai-Kolkata National Highways. On Tuesday, DRI officials spotted an ice cream vending vehicle parked near an ice manufacturing factory in Madhavaram, along the Chennai-Kolkata National Highway. The vehicle was reportedly waiting to load ice from the factory. items.title: Builder's RERA violations cannot make lenders criminally liable: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently held that violation of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA) by builders of a project cannot, by itself, form the basis for criminal prosecution of lenders who had extended loan facility to the builders for the concerned project [ Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited v. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta observed that the obligations under the relevant RERA provisions are primarily those of the promoter. "Alleged contraventions of RERA ... by themselves neither give rise to nor can they sustain prosecution for offences under the IPC. In particular, they cannot be made the foundation of a prosecution of a lender who is not the regulated entity, in the absence of the specific ingredients of the offence/s defined in IPC," the November 18 judgment stated. The Court also clarified that its earlier directions for preliminary enquiries by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into the builder-bank nexus in the National Capital Region (NCR) does not mean that lenders could be prosecuted merely because a developer had defaulted. items.title: Modification of arbitral awards: Not the need of the hour
items.summary: A recent column here made the case for a legislative amendment in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to provide courts with the power to modify awards in domestic arbitration. The column, in its conclusion, suggests that the scope of this amendment will be “ restricted to domestic India-seated awards falling foul of public policy ”. This essay is a response to the column and argues that India’s arbitration ecosystem requires a return to the basics, rather than reforms to appease the naysayers. Gayatri Balaswamy and its aftermath In the original column, the author covers the aftermath of the Supreme Court’s decision in Gayatri Balaswamy and how its unruly categories for when the power to modify is appropriate have led to more chaos than calm. Interestingly, the column makes the case for why the Supreme Court’s ability to modify the award under Article 142 will have "terrible consequences as a party will ultimately never be certain as to what the ultimate outcome will be (and whether an award will be modified eventually) (…) Businesses rely on certainty and predictability, and are loathe the use of unbridled discretion... ” I agree with this wholeheartedly. items.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp at Thiruparankundram as one time measure but stays Madras High Court observations
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday allowed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam as a one-time measure this year at the disputed stone pillar near the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy temple and the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on the Thiruparankundram hillock in Madurai. However, the Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi stayed observations made by the Madras High Court as regards the nature of the pillar and the land on which it stands. Worship at the customary sites and lawful access to the Dargah and mosque must continue undisturbed, the top court made it clear. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi The lamp can be lit only by a small team from the temple, the size and composition of which has to be decided by the Madurai District Collector in consultation with the temple Executive Officer, ASI and Police Commissioner. The Collector will supervise the arrangements and the police will provide security, with CRPF support if required and feasible, the Court said. "Public gatherings, processions, demonstrations and slogan-raising are barred at the site," the Bench underscored. items.title: How Deutsche Bank enabled money laundering and sanctioned oligarchs | South Central 102
items.summary: Can a global banking giant like Deutsche Bank be held accountable for allegedly enabling money laundering and hiding sanctioned oligarchs? What do 15.5 million leaked Deutsche Bank documents reveal about the bank’s role in the global financial system? Listen and follow on YouTube Listen and follow on Apple Listen and follow on Spotify In this week’s South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna examine a major international investigation into Deutsche Bank. They are joined by investigative journalist Josy Joseph, who led the investigation against Deutsche Bank. The investigation is based on approximately 15.5 million internal documents. Josy explains how the documents point to Deutsche Bank’s role in enabling sanctioned oligarchs to conceal their wealth and facilitating large-scale money laundering. He describes the bank as one of the central pieces of infrastructure in the global financial system, with its operations and correspondent banking networks spanning countries across the world. The conversation explores how financial institutions are supposed to identify suspicious transactions, why red flags can be overlooked, and how the pursuit of profit can take precedence

items.title: UoH students launch protest seeking professor’s termination over casteist remarks
items.summary: University of Hyderabad students have launched an indefinite protest demanding the termination of Dr Vijaya Ramdas Mandala, a faculty member in the History Department, over his alleged derogatory remarks about Dalit students in an email exchange. The remarks were allegedly made after a former student expressed hesitation regarding incorporating certain suggestions made by Vijaya Ramdas into his research because of ethical concerns. The incident took place in April but came to light only recently. The protest has been called by the Students’ Union, which comprises various student groups, including the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the Ambedkar Students’ Association, the Dalit Students’ Union,and the Tribal Students’ Forum. Students have been staging a sit-in outside the Social Sciences building, demanding Vijaya Ramdas’s termination. “We will not call off the protest until Vijaya Ramdas is terminated,” Students’ Union general secretary Aditya Rao told TNM. “We had protested earlier too, but no concrete action was taken against him,” he added.
